practices.practice: Create a single, process-wide MongoClient and reuse it (singleton) rather than creating a new client per request or per change-stream event.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single, long-lived MongoClient instance (singleton) per Node.js process; do not create a new client per request or per change-stream event.

practices.practice: Never store production DocumentDB credentials in code or the repo; read the connection string from environment variables and use a secrets store (for example, Azure Key Vault) in deployments, keeping only a .env.example with placeholders in source control.
practices.prior_belief: Never store DOCUMENTDB connection strings or credentials in code or repo; read them from environment variables (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and prefer a secrets store (Azure Key Vault) in deployments; include only a .env.example with placeholders.

practices.practice: Require TLS for all connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production; install/point to a CA bundle in restricted runtimes instead of relaxing verification.
practices.prior_belief: Require TLS/SSL for connections and enable server certificate validation in the MongoDB driver options (do not disable ssl/TLS verification in production).

practices.practice: Tune MongoClient connection options (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, maxIdleTimeMS) to your deployment pattern (serverless vs long-running) rather than relying on driver defaults.
practices.prior_belief: Configure sensible connection options on the MongoClient (maxPoolSize/minPoolSize, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, keepAlive) tuned for the workload rather than using driver defaults.

practices.practice: Enable driver retryable reads/writes where supported and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff for idempotent operations while avoiding infinite retries for non-idempotent side effects.
practices.prior_belief: Enable and rely on driver-level retryableReads/retryableWrites where available, and implement application-level exponential backoff for idempotent retries; avoid silent infinite retries for non-idempotent actions like sending messages.

practices.practice: Persist change-stream resume tokens (the _id from change events) to durable storage and resume streams using resumeAfter or startAtOperationTime to avoid missing or duplicating events after restarts.
practices.prior_belief: When using change streams, persist the latest resume token (or operationTime) to durable storage and on restart resume the stream from that token (resumeAfter/startAtOperationTime) to avoid missing or duplicating events.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB change streams resume token resumeAfter startAtOperationTime

practices.practice: Handle change-stream errors explicitly: persist resume progress frequently, attempt resumes for resumable/transient errors, and provide a safe recovery plan (for non-resumable errors) such as replaying a bounded time window; be aware of limitations such as topology changes and retention windows.
practices.prior_belief: Handle resumable and non-resumable change stream errors explicitly (catch resumable errors and attempt resume, persist resume tokens frequently, and in case of non-resumable errors fall back to a safe recovery plan such as re-reading a time-window of events).
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB change streams errors resumability limitations

practices.practice: Choose a shard/partition key with high cardinality and even distribution (for write-heavy workloads) or the most-frequent query filter (for read-heavy workloads); default to single-shard unless collection size or throughput exceeds one physical shard's budget.
practices.prior_belief: Choose a partition/shard key at collection creation with high cardinality and even distribution (e.g., customer_id) and declare it at creation time—do not rely on a collection being unpartitioned if you expect scale.

practices.practice: Create indexes for fields used in query predicates and sort keys and verify index usage with explain(); prefer targeted indexes rather than indexing every path by default.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes for every field used in query predicates and sort keys (e.g., customer_id, event_type, event_timestamp, outreach_status) and verify index usage with explain(); do index creation idempotently during app bootstrap.

practices.practice: Design compound indexes following the ESR (Equality → Sort → Range) rule so common query patterns are served by a single compound index rather than multiple single-field indexes.
practices.prior_belief: Create compound indexes that match common query patterns and field order (for example { customer_id:1, event_timestamp:-1 } for recent customer events) instead of relying on multiple single-field indexes.

practices.practice: Use projection to return only the fields needed for a query (for example exclude large payloads or embeddings) to reduce network transfer and RU/IO consumption.
practices.prior_belief: For queries that return large documents or many fields, use projection to return only the fields needed (e.g., exclude large embedding arrays unless required) to reduce network and RU/IO usage.
practices.source_name: Understand request units consumption in Azure Cosmos DB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB projection reduce RU network projection

practices.practice: Persist embeddings in a dedicated field and create a vector index with explicit parameters (dimensions, similarity, and index-type-specific tunables such as lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree or numLists) and tune both build- and search-time parameters for your accuracy/latency tradeoff.
practices.prior_belief: Persist embeddings in a dedicated field and create a vector index with explicit parameters (dimension, metric, and index tuning such as HNSW M/efConstruction or DiskANN/IVF params); set search-time ef/search parameters for accuracy/latency tradeoffs consistently between indexing and querying.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index create DiskANN HNSW IVF cosmosSearch

practices.practice: Normalize embedding vectors consistently at ingest (for example L2-normalize for COSine similarity) and store the embedding model name and dimensions with each document so you can detect drift and re-embed when models change.
practices.prior_belief: Normalize embedding vectors consistently (e.g., L2-normalize for cosine similarity) at write time and ensure the same normalization is applied to query vectors.

practices.practice: For temporary or retention-based logs use a TTL index on a timestamp field to automatically expire old records rather than relying on manual deletes.
practices.prior_belief: If outreach logs are temporary or subject to a retention policy, use a TTL index on a timestamp field to automatically expire old logs instead of manual deletes.

practices.practice: Make seeding and index-creation scripts idempotent: check for collection existence, use createIndexes (idempotent), or catch duplicate-key errors so running the script multiple times is safe.
practices.prior_belief: Make seeding and index-creation scripts idempotent: check for collection existence and use createIndexes (which is idempotent) or catch duplicate-key errors so running the script multiple times is safe.

practices.practice: Use multi-operation transactions only when you need atomicity across documents, keep transactions small and short-lived, and be prepared to retry transient transaction errors with exponential backoff.
practices.prior_belief: Use transactions only when you need atomic multi-document operations; keep transactions small and short-lived and be prepared to retry transient transaction errors with backoff.
practices.source_name: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Instrument and monitor cluster and query metrics (connections, pool usage, CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, slow query traces) and alert on leading indicators so you can scale or investigate before users are impacted.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and monitor database metrics (connection pool usage, active connections, ops/sec, latency, RU/sec or equivalent, index miss ratio) and capture slow query traces; use explain() to validate important queries in CI or during bootstrap.

practices.practice: Implement idempotency for external side effects (for example sending outreach): store and check an idempotency key such as event id or outreach_id in outreach_logs to avoid duplicate sends on replay.
practices.prior_belief: Implement idempotency for external side effects (e.g., sending outreach): include an idempotency key (event id, outreach_id) in outreach_logs and check it before sending to avoid duplicate messages if an event is replayed.

practices.practice: Persist change-stream consumer progress (resume tokens) durably so consumers can resume exactly where they left off, but do not rely on setting client-side writeConcern: Azure DocumentDB handles replication quorum for writes and client-specified writeConcern is ignored.
practices.prior_belief: Persist change-stream consumer progress (resume tokens, last processed event id/time) in a small, durable collection with a majority writeConcern so a crash or restart can resume exactly where it left off.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB change streams resume token writeConcern behavior

practices.practice: Avoid unbounded aggregations or map-reduce in change-stream consumers; process events in bounded batches, apply backpressure, and limit concurrency to avoid exhausting cluster throughput or overwhelming the database.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid unbounded aggregation or map-reduce on hot collections in the change-stream consumer; batch process events, apply backpressure, and limit concurrency to avoid overwhelming the DB or exceeding provisioned throughput.

practices.practice: Do not log full PII or credentials; redact or avoid persisting sensitive customer attributes in logs or persisted traces to meet security and compliance requirements.
practices.prior_belief: Do not log full PII or credentials; redact sensitive customer attributes in logs and in any persisted debug traces or stack dumps that could be stored in outreach_logs or monitoring exports.

notes: I inspected the app source to identify the areas it touches (connection handling, change-streams, seeding/indexing, message sending, logs) then used the installed DocumentDB skills and Microsoft Learn docs to discover public guidance. Each prior belief K01–K21 was checked against the public record: most were confirmed by DocumentDB-specific installed skills or Microsoft Learn pages; K19 (client-enforced majority writeConcern) was contradicted by Azure DocumentDB documentation which states the service handles quorum and client writeConcern may be ignored.
